correctness.rationale: Source convergence follows from primitivity and the sink has a stable linear recurrence for every positive coupling, even when S is periodic. For 0<a<b<=1 the algebraic resolvent identity may be written K=F_a F_b^(-1)=lambda I+(1−lambda)F_a with lambda=a(1−b)/(b(1−a)) in [0,1). The Neumann series makes F_a strictly positive on any irreducible S, and its row sums and left stationary weights are preserved. This includes b=1, when K=F_a. Jensen is strict in every row for a strictly convex test unless h_b is constant, equivalently w is constant by F_b's invertibility and constant preservation. The all-source-vector consensus criterion follows by testing the coordinate source vectors, realizable by constant initial opinions. Restricting I−S to the invariant pi-mean-zero subspace gives the Poisson inverse irrespective of periodicity and the stated small-rate expansion; it does not identify the dynamics at zero coupling. Direct scalar elimination in the three-node example gives h_(1/5)=(111/125,1618/1625,111/3250), h_(4/5)=(597/1000,400597/401000,597/401000). Unweighted variances are 14071/76050 > 6075272/36180225, while stationary-weighted variances are 1562779/169000000 < 114272491/10050062500. The stationary mean is 197/200 for both. The periodic two-vertex swap independently checks the endpoint and shows the nonconstant difference is scaled by e/(2−e).
residual_risks: Finite checks corroborate the rational example and a periodic boundary case only. The full strict-order statement is analytical and requires shared scalar coupling, irreducibility, and nonconstant w for strict tests.

This is an elementary but useful application of the resolvent identity; the identity, Jensen, equilibrium resolvent, heterogeneous disagreement, and existence of an ordinary-variance reversal in a related subfamily are not new. value.rationale: The common parameter is a natural modeling control, and the proposition supplies a distribution-wide and graph-independent ordering rather than only a single scalar warning. A single strictly positive Markov factor gives sharp equality conditions and extends the asymmetric-network comparison even when spectral variance arguments based on reversibility cannot apply. The weighting caveat is pedagogically useful but already known in an overlapping subfamily; it is not the distinct scientific increment.
residual_risks: The contribution is modest; no inference is warranted for observed polarization, independent coupling variations, signed influences, or cyclic multiplex feedback.
